tagline: Every spec sheet is a marketing document. We read the standard instead.

author.name: The SpecWire Desk
author.bio: SpecWire does not run a hardware lab, and says so plainly. What it does is read the documents almost nobody reads end to end - the standards, the compliance test specs, the panel and silicon datasheets, the model cards, the manufacturer spec pages - and reconcile them against what the marketing says. Where a number comes from a measurement, we name the lab that took it. Every figure carries the revision it came from and the date it was current.

footer_blurb: Independent tech explainers and review round-ups. We trace phone, laptop, display and AI claims back to the datasheet, the standard or the lab that measured them - and we cite all three.
disclaimer_line: Nothing here replaces testing your own unit, and silicon behaviour varies between production runs and firmware revisions

homepage.title: SpecWire - tech specs, decoded and fact-checked
homepage.meta: Plain-English explainers and review round-ups for phones, laptops, displays and AI. What each spec measures, who certifies it, and which numbers matter.
homepage.h1: The number on the box, and the number that matters
homepage.dek: Most tech specifications are self-reported, measured however the manufacturer prefers, and quoted without the conditions that make them meaningful. SpecWire reads the standards and the independent lab data, then tells you which claims actually hold.

not_found_meta: We could not find that page. Browse SpecWire's explainers and review round-ups on phones, laptops, displays and AI instead.
llms_blurb: Independent, source-traced explainers and review round-ups covering smartphones, laptops, displays, AI models and consumer audio.
sourcing_note: Claims are traced to primary sources - standards-body compliance documents, silicon and panel datasheets, manufacturer specification pages, published model cards and named independent lab measurements - with the revision and the date the figure was current. SpecWire does not operate its own test lab and never presents third-party measurements as its own. Review round-ups summarise and link to the outlets that did the testing, and are labelled as such. Content is drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by a human editor; see /editorial-policy/.

factcheck.note: Every post carries per-figure source indices; validate.py fails the build otherwise. A primary source here means a standards-body compliance document (VESA, HDMI Forum, USB-IF, Bluetooth SIG, JEDEC, ITU-R), a silicon or panel datasheet, a manufacturer specification page, a published model card, or a named independent lab's own measurement.
